knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: Prime(2^n−1)→Prime(n) fully verified in Lean (0 axioms, 0 sorries, Docker build OK, #print axioms = propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound only). Gallery entry + PR.
insights: Contrapositive on the exponent: if 2^n−1 is prime but n is composite (n≥2), a proper divisor 2≤d<n lifts to a proper Mersenne divisor 2^d−1 of 2^n−1, contradicting primality.
Key Mathlib lift: Nat.pow_sub_one_dvd_pow_sub_one (m∣k → x^m−1 ∣ x^k−1), a corollary of x−y ∣ xⁿ−yⁿ (Nat.sub_dvd_pow_sub_pow, now in Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.GeomSum, not GeomSum).
Both boundary escapes (2^d−1=1 and 2^d−1=2^n−1) close via Nat.pow_right_injective (2≤a → Injective (a^·)): 2^d=2 forces d=1, 2^d=2^n forces d=n.
Converse is false: 2^11−1 = 2047 = 23·89, so prime exponent is necessary but not sufficient — the fact that lets Lucas–Lehmer restrict to prime exponents.
mathlibGaps: Mathlib has the Mersenne definition and Lucas–Lehmer machinery but does not expose the necessary-condition lemma Prime(2^n−1)→Prime(n) as a standalone named result.
nextSteps: Follow-up (open): does the same exponent-divisibility lift give a short proof that a Fermat prime 2^n+1 forces n to be a power of 2 (odd-divisor obstruction 2^d+1 ∣ 2^n+1 for odd d∣n)?
Follow-up: strengthen toward q ≡ 1 (mod 2p) and q ≡ ±1 (mod 8) for prime factors q of 2^p−1.
